feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. Iteration 2 (lead y = 0.07 m, controller unchanged) gave the best score so far, 60.41, up from 52.33 at lead 0.05 m. The gain came from the oval, where progress rose from 0.112 to 0.168 and max_error stayed near 0.063. The slalom (progress 0.110) and s-bend (progress 0.160) did not change, and both still end off track. Iteration 1 showed the s-bend progress was also 0.160 at lead 0.05 m, so the s-bend is not limited by lead. Depending on the next race: if the oval progress rises again and slalom steering_oscillation stays near the iteration 2 level of about 0.15, keep lead 0.08 m and move to the spacing or speed levers. If slalom oscillation rises clearly above about 0.16 while max_error falls, lead is overshooting, so use y = 0.075 m. If progress and max_error are within about 0.01 of iteration 2 on all tracks, lead has stopped being the limit, and the next change should be wheel_radius or sensor spacing.
requested_changes: If lead 0.08 m leaves the s-bend at progress 0.16 with max_error near 0.061-0.069 m (the same as leads 0.05 and 0.07 m), try wheel_radius 0.035 m. The s-bend result has not moved with lead (iterations 1 and 2 both 0.160), and no iteration has yet tested speed, which the 3 s finish limit needs.

If line_loss_events rise above 1 on the s-bend or slalom at max_error 0.06-0.07 m, narrow the outer sensors to x = +/-0.02 m (10 mm spacing) so they stay on the 25 mm tape. Iteration 2 showed line loss still at 1 per run, so this is only a fallback.

If slalom steering_oscillation rises above about 0.16 at lead 0.08 m (iteration 2 slalom was 0.149), move the lead back to y = 0.075 m, or raise wheel_track to 0.11 m to reduce yaw gain. Both are supported by the iteration 2 oscillation data.
